short: A classical Greek philosopher credited as one of the founders of Western philosophy, known for his method of questioning.
full:
Socrates spent his life in Athens engaging citizens in rigorous dialogues, questioning their fundamental assumptions about justice, virtue, and knowledge. He wrote nothing down; his thoughts and methods survive entirely through the accounts of his students, most notably Plato and Xenophon. His relentless questioning, known as the Socratic method, laid the groundwork for formal logic and ethics.

His association with critics of the Athenian democracy and his habit of exposing the ignorance of powerful figures made him deeply unpopular. In 399 BCE, he was put on trial for corrupting the youth and impiety, convicted, and sentenced to death by drinking hemlock.
